text:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a 'soft onramp' for new tenants to reduce cold-start abuse. Idea: give a small burst pool for first N minutes tied to behavioral signals, then auto-transition into regular quotas. Looking for thoughts on interface boundaries (ingress -> admission -> quota) and obvious attack vectors.

samir: Nice. Main risk is churn abuse: attacker creates many tenants to harvest bursts. How do we tie the onramp to something hard to spoof? billing, org age, fingerprints?

tess: For self-serve, we should do progressive ramping rather than a single big burst. e.g. initial cap 2k tokens, then increase after several low-anomaly windows. For higher burst we require billing verification.

maya: Sketching an interface idea: admission API returns an onramp grant blob so callers don't have to implement logic. e.g. response contains onramp_grant: {allowed: true, tokens: 2000, expires_at: <ts>, telemetry_id: "onramp-abc"} — admission owns lifecycle.

ev an: Where do abuse signals live today? our abuse-detector is async and batched, so admission can't get a fresh score on every request without adding latency.

samir: We can use a hybrid: cached score with TTL + fast heuristics in admission (sudden churn, ip velocity). If cached score > threshold, deny onramp.

tess: Tradeoffs: sync checks increase p99 for new tenants. I prefer cached + bloom-style fast checks. Also add a penalty weight on the onramp token bucket so abuse drains it faster.

maya: Example response shape (proto):
```
{
  "onramp_grant": true,
  "tokens": 2000,
  "window_secs": 600,
  "escalate_after_windows": 3,
  "telemetry_id": "onramp-2026-03"
}
```
This keeps admission -> quota service boundary simple: admission issues grant, quota enforces counts.

ev an: For signals: we should send a sync hint: admission can ask a short-lived 'risk_token' from abuse service (fast path) and include in grant. Abuse service keeps lightweight cache keyed by org_id.

samir: Ops ask: what metrics do we need? onramp_hits, onramp_rejections, escalations, per-tenant burst_consumed, reenabled_by_human. Need dashboards + alerts if >X rejections per minute.

maya: Rollout plan: behind feature-flag, enable for internal/test orgs, then small % of new signups. Auto-disable per-org on suspicious signals. Add runbook: how to revoke grants and escalate to SRE.

infra-bot: deploybot: starting rollout of feature-flag redwood.onramp.v1 -> staging :rocket:

samir: Also add a backstop: global guard in our edge proxy that caps onramp rate per-IP/network to catch mass-tenant creation from same source.

tess: Agreed. I'll help write the RFC and the sample dashboard. @maya please add the API proto + a quick simulation of burst economics.

maya: Will do — drafting now and tagging you both. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
